# Catalyze Care

> Catalyze Care is a healthcare marketing agency for therapy practices, psychiatry clinics, and multi-location specialty groups. We help practices get more patients from the doctors who already refer in their market, then add SEO and paid ads on the same plan, at published prices.

Key facts
- Services: healthcare referral marketing (flagship), SEO for healthcare practices, paid ads (Google Ads, Meta Ads, Display) for healthcare practices.
- Published prices: referral marketing $5,000/month with a 3-month minimum; SEO $799/month with a 6-month minimum; paid ads management $2,500/month plus media, with a 3-month minimum.
- Who we work with: therapy practices, psychiatry clinics, multi-location mental health groups, and other specialty practices and provider groups in the US.
- Referral outreach channels: fax, email, phone, LinkedIn, and direct mail to offices that already refer in your specialty.
- Reporting: monthly, tied to booked appointments from your intake, not clicks.
- Client results are published only with the client’s written permission.
- Pricing: https://catalyzegrowth.co/pricing
- Content feed (JSON Feed, every live page and post with its last update): https://catalyzegrowth.co/feed.json
- Contact: andrew@catalyzegrowth.co. Book a demo: https://catalyzegrowth.co/#contact

## Guides
- What Is a Healthcare Marketing Agency?: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/what-is-a-healthcare-marketing-agency
  A healthcare marketing agency runs referral marketing, SEO, and paid ads for practices, with patient-facing pages written for the specialty and geography, published fees, and tracking that keeps PHI off ad platforms.
- SEO for Healthcare Practices, Explained: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/seo-for-healthcare-practices-explained
  SEO for healthcare practices covers Google Business Profile, citations, on-page and technical work, schema, and patient-facing content written for your specialty and geography.
- Paid Ads for Healthcare Practices, Explained: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/paid-ads-for-healthcare-practices-explained
  Paid ads for healthcare practices are Google Ads, Meta Ads, and Display campaigns aimed at booked appointments. Management is $2,500 a month plus media. Common questions cover setup timing, what the fee covers versus media, campaign types, tracking to booked visits, and HIPAA-aware tracking.
- Healthcare Referral Marketing Explained | Claims-Backed Playbook: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/what-is-healthcare-referral-marketing
- What a Physician Referral Marketing Agency Does Each Month: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/physician-referral-marketing-agency
  Finds offices that already send the specialty, runs outreach on the channels those offices use, and reports booked appointments from intake. $5,000/month, 3-month minimum.
- What to Check When Referral Volume Dips: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/when-referral-volume-dips-healthcare-practices
  When referrals fall, check four things before you change vendors: whether your target list still matches who sends your specialty, whether someone closes the loop within seven days, whether outreach is still reaching those offices, and whether intake can take the next patient. A dip is usually one of those four, and your own fields show which.
- Google Ads vs Meta Ads for a Healthcare Practice: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/healthcare-google-ads-vs-meta-ads-for-practices
  Use Google Ads when people are searching for care in your area. Use Meta Ads to reach people in your service area who are not searching yet, without targeting a condition. A contents list covers when each platform fits and what the $2,500 fee includes.
- Healthcare Digital Marketing, Explained: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/healthcare-digital-marketing-explained
  Healthcare digital marketing is SEO, paid ads, and referral outreach on one plan. SEO includes patient-facing content written for the specialty and geography.
- Referral Marketing vs Paid Ads for Healthcare Practices: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/provider-referrals-vs-paid-ads
  Referral marketing reaches the offices that already send patients in your specialty. Paid ads buy nearer-term demand from people searching for care, and stop when spend stops. Fees are $5,000/month and $2,500/month plus media.
- Fax Isn't Dead: Why It Still Works for Reaching Physician Offices in 2026: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/fax-marketing-physician-offices
- Voicemail Drops, TCPA, and Healthcare Outreach: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/ringless-voicemail-tcpa-healthcare-outreach
  Scrub line type, keep the message informational, and treat wireless prerecorded drops as TCPA-covered calls, not a shortcut around consent.
- How to Build a Referral Target List That Actually Produces Referrals: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/build-physician-referral-target-list
  Start from the patient journey: list every provider who sees your patient before you do. Filter to the area you actually serve, rank by referral volume, and find the person in each office who routes referrals. Catalyze Care uses this method inside referral marketing at $5,000/month.
- LinkedIn Outreach to Physicians: The Message That Gets Replies: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/linkedin-outreach-physicians-referrals
  Use LinkedIn as a later, specific touch inside a referral program, not as a broadcast pitch. $5,000/month, 3-month minimum.
- Google Ads for Healthcare: LegitScript and Disapprovals: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/google-ads-healthcare-2026-legitscript
  Treat Google Ads for healthcare as a certification and policy question first. Confirm whether your category needs LegitScript before you scale. Catalyze Care runs paid ads management at $2,500/month plus media.
- Meta Ads for Healthcare: You Can't Target by Condition: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/meta-ads-healthcare-without-condition-targeting
  On Meta, target by broad geography and life stage, and let creative that names the service draw the right people. Condition-based audiences are gone. See Catalyze Care paid ads for campaign management.
- HIPAA and Marketing Pixels: What Changed: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/hipaa-marketing-pixels-tracking
  Measure appointments and inquiries while keeping protected health information out of the pixels, tags, and web addresses sent to ad platforms. The risk is sending an identifier together with health, care, or payment context, so keep those two apart.
- Local SEO for Multi-State Telehealth: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/local-seo-multi-state-telehealth
  Build one real page for each state you are licensed in, with the services, insurance, clinicians licensed there, and telehealth logistics that actually differ by state. Name your licensed service area.
- How to Get Your Practice Cited in AI Search: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/ai-search-healthcare-practice-visibility
  You earn citations in AI search by answering the patient’s question up front, keeping your facts consistent with your Google Business Profile and directories, and showing a named clinician. Answer engines quote sources they can check.
- The Pediatrician Channel: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/pediatrician-referrals-behavioral-health-therapy
  Reach the pediatric offices that already see children who later need behavioral health, ABA, speech, or OT. Become the practice they trust to see the child soon, take the payer, and send a closed-loop note after the first visit. Referral marketing is $5,000/month with a 3-month minimum.
- Q4 Is Not Dead: Deductible Resets, Open Enrollment, and Planning for January Demand: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/healthcare-marketing-q4-january-demand
  Use Q4 to get ready for January, when plans reset and deductibles change. Update your directory listings and insurance information, confirm intake can handle higher call volume, refresh your referring-office outreach, and build paid campaigns so they launch before demand rises.
- What Does It Cost to Acquire a Patient?: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/patient-acquisition-cost-benchmarks
  Patient acquisition cost is your marketing spend divided by the new patients who complete intake, using the booked field your front desk already records. Use published fees as the inputs: referral $5,000/month, SEO $799/month, and paid ads management $2,500/month plus media.
- Your Directory Profiles Are Losing You Patients: A 30-Minute Audit: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/healthcare-directory-profile-audit
  Spend thirty minutes checking the listings a patient or referral coordinator sees first: your Google Business Profile, your top payer directories, and the specialty listings that matter in your market. Confirm your name, address, and phone match across all of them.
- The Six-Touch Nurture Cadence: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/referral-nurture-cadence-referring-offices
  Keep referring offices with a scheduled set of useful contacts: a first-visit note, quarterly capacity updates, a clinical insight piece, a personal check-in for top referrers, a fading-referrer call, and a year-end thank-you. Every touch gives the office something they can use. The cadence runs inside referral marketing.
- Your 2027 Healthcare Marketing Plan on One Page: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/2027-healthcare-marketing-plan-template
  Put your 2027 plan on one page with five parts: a numeric target, three named channels with an owner and budget each, five monthly numbers you check against intake, a calendar, and a compliance line. Review it every month against your own intake.
- SEO vs GEO for Healthcare Practices: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/seo-vs-geo-healthcare-practices
  SEO is how patients find you in Google’s regular results and the Maps block when they search for your specialty nearby. GEO is earning citations when AI Overviews and answer engines write an answer. SEO scope includes patient-facing content written for the specialty and geography.
- Agency vs In-House Healthcare Marketing: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/agency-vs-in-house-healthcare-marketing
  Choose in-house when you have steady work for one or two channels, clinical review capacity, and a manager with time to coach. Choose an agency when you need specialist referral, SEO, or paid ads work without hiring for each role.
- Physician Liaison vs Referral Agency: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/physician-liaison-vs-referral-agency
  A physician liaison is a relationship role that visits referring offices in person, resolves access issues, and grows volume for your organization. A referral agency runs multi-channel outreach by email, phone, LinkedIn, and mail against a claims-backed list and reports every month.
- HIPAA-Aware Google Ads Conversion Tracking for Practices: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/hipaa-google-ads-conversion-tracking
  Track the appointment request, not the diagnosis. Keep patient details out of pixels, tags, and URLs, and count conversions your front desk can confirm. A contents list covers what OCR flagged, practical conversion rules, and sources. Paid ads management is $2,500/month plus media.
- Local SEO Checklist for Healthcare Practices: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/local-seo-checklist-healthcare-practices
  A local SEO checklist for healthcare practices: Google Business Profile, matching name, address, and phone, reviews, citations, on-page basics, and patient-facing content written for the specialty and geography.
- Google Business Profile for Healthcare Practices: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/google-business-profile-healthcare-practices
  Your Google Business Profile should match the clinic door, the website, and the directories: same name, address, phone, hours, and services. A contents list points to the profile steps, one listing per staffed location, reviews, and schema that matches the page.
- When Not to Hire a Healthcare Marketing Agency: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/when-not-to-hire-healthcare-marketing-agency
  Hire an agency when intake can take the next patient and leadership will name who you take. Skip it when the only ask is a promised ranking or return, or when the real job is hospital leakage analytics or a logo-only project.
- Questions Before Signing a Healthcare Marketing Contract: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/questions-before-signing-healthcare-marketing-contract
  Before you sign, lock four things in writing: who owns the data and accounts, how HIPAA-aware tracking is set up, what the monthly report contains, and how cancel or pause works. Put them in the same document as the fee.
- Multi-Location vs Single-Site Healthcare SEO: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/multi-location-vs-single-site-healthcare-seo
  Both share one truth test: your name, address, and phone must match the real clinic everywhere they appear. A single site runs one Google Business Profile and one public address. Each staffed location needs its own profile.
- How to Read a Healthcare Marketing Agency Proposal: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/how-to-read-healthcare-marketing-agency-proposal
  A proposal is complete when four things sit in the same document as the fee: who owns the accounts and lists, how HIPAA-aware tracking is set up, what the monthly report contains, and how cancel or pause works. If any are missing, ask the vendor to add them before you sign.
- Close-the-Loop Referral Reporting for Practices: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/close-the-loop-referral-reporting
  Close-the-loop referral reporting is a monthly packet you can check against intake: which offices were contacted, which responded, which patients named a referring provider, and whether those offices got an acknowledgment. Count only what your front desk can confirm.
- Google Ads Account Structure for Healthcare Practices: https://catalyzegrowth.co/blog/google-ads-account-structure-healthcare-practices
